page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c1.small is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU hardware, requiring external block storage for operating system and application deployment.

A key technical characteristic of the ecs.c1.small is the absence of several modern CPU instruction set extensions. The underlying processor configuration does not support Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), or hardware-accelerated cryptography flags such as AES and SHA_NI. Additionally, virtualization extensions (VMX/SVM) and hyper-threading (HT) flags are not exposed to the guest OS. These omissions limit the instance's suitability for workloads relying heavily on vector math, machine learning inference, or hardware-based encryption.

From a resource allocation perspective, the ecs.c1.small offers a compute-heavy profile with a low memory-to-CPU ratio. This makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints or advanced instruction sets. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, lightweight batch processing, and simple computational tasks that fit within the 8.0 GB memory boundary.
